idea-plugin.name: IDE Pilot MCP
idea-plugin.description:
IDE Pilot MCP lets AI agents see and use your IDE's UI like a user: read windows, dialogs and editors, click, type, run actions, and read consoles and test results. Playwright MCP for JetBrains IDEs: a Model Context Protocol server for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and other agents.

Use it to test your plugin's UI end to end in the runIde sandbox, reproduce bug reports, check dialogs, settings and quick fixes, run tests and read their failures, or rerun your running application after a change (or HotSwap it into a debug session) and wait until its console says it started. It drives the UI, which makes it a good companion to code-level MCP servers.

Tools

  • pilot_action – runs an IDE action by ID, optionally in a Run/Debug tab by name, and returns what it showed (hints, popups, dialogs, notifications), or finds actions by ID or menu text.
  • pilot_click – clicks the component or row with a ref: left, middle or right button, double-click, with modifier keys; or hovers over it to show tooltips, or drags it onto another ref; optionally returns what it showed, as pilot_action does.
  • pilot_editor – reads an editor's text, caret and problems, moves its caret, and lists or applies its Alt+Enter actions.
  • pilot_evaluate – runs a Groovy script inside the IDE, or in a running Java debug session with its JDI VirtualMachine bound.
  • pilot_memory – live instances per class in a running Java debug session or Run tab, their growth since a baseline, and, from a heap dump, the chain of references keeping an instance alive, with the JDK's classes optionally hidden: leak detection without a profiler.
  • pilot_log – the idea.log tail, the IDE's caught exceptions, recent UI freezes, notifications, stdout/stderr, or Run/Debug sessions (mode, state, process ID) and their console text, and Terminal tabs, or test run results (counts, failed tests with message and stack), by tab name or running only.
  • pilot_open – opens a project, or a file at a line.
  • pilot_screenshot – PNG of a component, or of the active window with its popups.
  • pilot_scroll – scrolls a scroll pane by pages or to its top or bottom, or a list, tree or table to the row with some text.
  • pilot_settings – effective values, defaults included, of registry keys, of an Advanced Setting by its ID and of a service's persisted settings by its class name.
  • pilot_snapshot – the visible UI as a text tree of windows, components, list, tree and table rows, and Compose (Jewel) UI, with role, name, state and a ref to act on; paged, optionally with screen positions, and optionally with every row of lists, trees and tables, not only those that show; or only the windows (active, maximized, modal, indexing) and screens.
  • pilot_type – types text and presses keys, optionally replacing the content; shortcuts run their actions; selects combo box items by text; holds modifier keys down across calls until released.
  • pilot_window – brings a window to the front, maximizes, restores, resizes, moves or closes it, and moves or detaches tool windows.
  • pilot_wait_for – waits for text to show or go, for indexing, background tasks or a Gradle/Maven sync to finish, for new Run console or Terminal output (returning the matching lines), or for a time.

The server listens on localhost and needs a token: generate it in Settings | Tools | IDE Pilot and paste it into the agent's MCP settings.
